answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to prove a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with every result needed before the next begins. A verifier checks the final Wesolowski proof efficiently, but an attacker simulating many clones cannot parallelize any one chain across GPUs: hardware can run chains concurrently, yet cannot reduce per-identity latency. Thus jade, nadir, and knoll challenges impose a strict physical time bottleneck.
